summary: This benchmark investigates the causal impact of token ordering on internal representation steering in Qwen2.5-72B by moving a key assignment relative to a dictionary definition. Using full-state activation swapping at layer 17 across 256 program groups, the study demonstrates that late key placement increases intervention switching fidelity from 74 to 138 out of 139 shared-native groups, albeit with a drop in baseline native accuracy. The methodology is statistically sound and hardware/environment reporting is exceptionally precise.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design with counterfactual controls, including mirrored context switching, constant-table preservation tests, and cohort isolation.
Comprehensive statistical reporting including paired lift calculations and 95% confidence intervals (+46.04 pp, [38.13, 53.96]).
Exemplary reproducibility documentation specifying exact software versions (MLX 0.32.4, NumPy 2.5.5, macOS 27.2), hardware specifications (M5 Ultra 80-core GPU, 256 GiB), and verification commands.
Careful separation of native model accuracy degradation from causal intervention reliability within the shared-native cohort.
weaknesses: Evaluates only a single intervention depth (after block 17) rather than sweeping across layers to establish whether layer 17 represents an optimal causal bottleneck.
The scope is restricted to a single model family (Qwen2.5-72B) and a narrow synthetic Python lookup task, limiting cross-architecture generalization.
The reduction in native accuracy (from 183/256 to 155/256) when relocating the key is not qualitatively analyzed.
suggestions: Perform a layer sweep across intermediate blocks (e.g., layers 10 through 40) to determine how layer depth interacts with token distance in causal activation exchange.
Analyze the failure cases in the native accuracy reduction to explain why post-dictionary key placement degrades baseline completion performance.
Replicate the benchmark on additional open-weight models of varying scales (e.g., Llama-3.3-70B or Qwen2.5-32B) to assess generality.

claims.text: The only tested intervention exchanges the full 8,192-value state at the key token between the two versions of a prompt after 17 blocks in frozen BF16 Qwen2.5-72B.
The Studio run took 249 seconds with 146.70 GB peak MLX allocation on Apple M5 Ultra with 80 GPU cores and 256 GiB unified memory.
It used macOS 27.2 (26B118), Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2, NumPy 2.5.5 and tokenizers 0.23.3.
